subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 28-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation presents with regular uterine contractions and cervical change consistent with preterm labor. Her physician orders a tocolytic that is a beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist to relax uterine smooth muscle.
question: Which of the following tocolytics is a beta-2 agonist?
explanation_correct: Terbutaline is a beta-2 adrenergic agonist used as a tocolytic; stimulation of beta-2 receptors relaxes uterine smooth muscle and reduces contraction frequency. It is one of the tocolytics captured by the mnemonic 'Keep baby in the TIN' (Terbutaline, Indomethacin, Nifedipine). Indomethacin is an NSAID and nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker.

explanation_incorrect.A: Indomethacin is an NSAID used as a tocolytic, not a beta-2 agonist.
explanation_incorrect.B: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker used as a tocolytic, not a beta-2 agonist.
explanation_incorrect.C: Magnesium sulfate is not one of the TIN tocolytics; it is used in preeclampsia and eclampsia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Oxytocin promotes uterine contractions and is used to induce or augment labor, the opposite of a tocolytic.

educationalObjective: Terbutaline is the beta-2 agonist tocolytic, one of the 'TIN' drugs (Terbutaline, Indomethacin, Nifedipine).

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 31-year-old woman at 29 weeks' gestation with preterm labor is given a tocolytic that works by inhibiting cyclooxygenase and reducing prostaglandin synthesis. The goal is to relax the uterus and decrease the frequency of contractions.
question: Which of the following tocolytics acts as an NSAID?
explanation_correct: Indomethacin is an NSAID that reduces prostaglandin synthesis and is used as a tocolytic to relax the uterus and decrease contraction frequency in preterm labor. Terbutaline is a beta-2 agonist and nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker; together with indomethacin they form the 'TIN' mnemonic (Terbutaline, Indomethacin, Nifedipine) to keep the baby in.

explanation_incorrect.B: Terbutaline is a beta-2 adrenergic agonist, not an NSAID.
explanation_incorrect.C: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker, not an NSAID.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ritodrine is a beta-2 agonist tocolytic, not an NSAID.
explanation_incorrect.E: Oxytocin stimulates uterine contractions and is not a tocolytic at all.

educationalObjective: Indomethacin is the NSAID tocolytic; terbutaline and ritodrine are beta-2 agonists and nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 33-year-old woman in preterm labor is started on a tocolytic that blocks calcium channels, reducing calcium influx into uterine smooth muscle and lowering contraction frequency. The team is also preparing to give antenatal corticosteroids.
question: Which of the following is this calcium channel blocker tocolytic?
explanation_correct: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker used as a tocolytic; by blocking calcium influx into uterine smooth muscle it reduces the frequency of contractions in preterm labor. It is part of the 'TIN' mnemonic (Terbutaline, Indomethacin, Nifedipine) summarized as 'Keep baby in the TIN.' Tocolytics buy time for glucocorticoids to promote fetal lung maturity or for transfer to an appropriate center.

explanation_incorrect.A: Indomethacin is an NSAID that reduces prostaglandin synthesis, not a calcium channel blocker.
explanation_incorrect.B: Terbutaline is a beta-2 adrenergic agonist, not a calcium channel blocker.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ritodrine is a beta-2 agonist, not a calcium channel blocker.
explanation_incorrect.D: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin analog used for medical termination and postpartum hemorrhage, not a tocolytic calcium channel blocker.

educationalObjective: Nifedipine is the calcium channel blocker tocolytic that relaxes uterine smooth muscle by blocking calcium influx.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A woman at 27 weeks' gestation presents with regular uterine contractions and cervical change consistent with preterm labor. The neonatology team wants to use the delay gained from tocolysis to administer antenatal corticosteroids before delivery.
question: What is the primary goal of tocolytic therapy in this setting?

options.text: To permanently arrest labor so the pregnancy can continue to term
To reduce contraction frequency, allowing time for glucocorticoids to promote fetal lung maturity and transfer to a center with obstetric care
To directly induce fetal lung maturation
To accelerate delivery for maternal indications
To treat the underlying cause of the preterm labor

explanation_correct: Tocolytics (terbutaline, indomethacin, nifedipine, remembered as 'Keep baby in the TIN') relax the uterus and reduce contraction frequency in preterm labor. Their purpose is not to stop labor permanently but to buy time, typically to administer glucocorticoids that promote fetal lung maturity and to arrange transfer to a center with appropriate obstetrical care. They do not treat the underlying cause of preterm labor.

explanation_incorrect.A: Tocolytics only temporarily delay delivery; they do not provide permanent arrest of labor and are not a long-term solution.
explanation_incorrect.C: Tocolytics do not directly mature fetal lungs; they allow time for antenatal glucocorticoids to do so.
explanation_incorrect.D: Accelerating delivery is the opposite of tocolysis and would be achieved with induction or augmentation agents.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tocolytics relax uterine smooth muscle but do not address underlying causes such as infection or abruption.

educationalObjective: Tocolytics temporarily reduce preterm contractions to allow glucocorticoids for fetal lung maturity and transfer to an appropriate center, not to stop labor permanently.
